title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 52 (Application of Premiums Received on Issue of Shares)

content.overview: Section 52 requires that where a company issues shares at a premium, whether for cash or otherwise, a sum equal to the aggregate amount or value of the premiums on those shares be transferred to a securities premium account. The section restricts the application of that account to specified purposes such as issuing fully paid bonus shares, writing off preliminary expenses, writing off expenses of issue or commission/discount on issue of shares or debentures, providing for premium payable on redemption of preference shares or debentures, and buy-back under section 68.
content.glance: Premiums go to securities premium account; application limited to statutory purposes (bonus shares, write-offs, redemption premium, buy-back).
content.study: Where a company issues shares at a premium, whether for cash or otherwise, a sum equal to the aggregate amount or value of the premiums on those shares shall be transferred to a ‘securities premium account’. The securities premium account may be applied only for the purposes specified in the section: issuing fully paid bonus shares; writing off the preliminary expenses of the company; writing off the expenses of, or the commission paid or discount allowed on, any issue of shares or debentures; providing for the premium payable on the redemption of any redeemable preference shares or of any debentures; or purchase of its own shares or other securities under section 68. Current-law framing: identify issue at premium; transfer to securities premium account; restrict application to listed purposes.

sections.heading: Transfer to Securities Premium Account
sections.body: Aggregate premiums on shares issued at a premium must be transferred to the securities premium account.

sections.heading: Permitted Applications
sections.body: Bonus shares; write-off of preliminary expenses; write-off of issue expenses/commission/discount; premium on redemption of preference shares or debentures; buy-back under s. 68.

sections.heading: Restriction
sections.body: The account cannot be applied for purposes outside the statutory list.

provisions.title: Application of premiums received on issue of shares

examples.title: Bonus from premium
examples.body: The company issues fully paid bonus shares by capitalising the securities premium account. Section 52 permits this application.

examples.title: Impermissible use
examples.body: The company tries to distribute securities premium as ordinary dividend. Section 52 does not permit that application.

hypotheticals.question: Can securities premium be used to pay ordinary dividends?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 52 limits application to the listed purposes; ordinary dividend is not among them.

distinctions.title: Securities premium (s. 52) vs prohibition on discount (s. 53)
distinctions.left: Accounting and restricted use of premium
distinctions.right: Ban on issuing shares at a discount (with limited exceptions)

misconceptions.trap: Securities premium is free reserves available for any purpose.
misconceptions.correction: Section 52 restricts application to specified purposes only.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 52 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify issue at premium. II. Confirm transfer to securities premium account. III. Test proposed application against the statutory list. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Premium facts; account balance; proposed use; statutory permission or prohibition; precise relief.

examTips: List the permitted applications of securities premium.
Emphasise that the list is exhaustive for ordinary application.
